parts.title: 大問1 短文の語句空所補充
parts.desc: 短い文や会話の空所に入る単語・熟語・文法を4つから選ぶ
parts.tip: 空所の前後で品詞と形（後ろに to や from が来るか）を見て、2文目で意味のヒント（理由・結果・but の対比）を探す。熟語は前置詞までセットで覚える。文法は時制を示す語（ago・ever）や if の形が決め手。
parts.intro: Read each item and choose the word or phrase that best fills the blank.

questions.q: The hotel staff were very ____ to us. They carried our bags to our room and told us about some good restaurants near the hotel.
questions.why: helpful＝「親切な・役に立つ」。荷物を運び、店を教えてくれた、という2文目と合う。narrow（狭い）、ancient（古代の）、empty（空の）は人の態度を表さない。
questions.ja: ホテルのスタッフは私たちにとても（　）だった。部屋まで荷物を運び、ホテルの近くの良いレストランを教えてくれた。

questions.q: Before the trip, Kenji made a ____ at a small hotel near the beach. He wanted to be sure that he had a room for three nights.
questions.why: make a reservation＝「予約する」。3泊分の部屋を確保したかった、という2文目がヒント。temperature（温度）、signal（合図）、direction（方向）はホテルと結びつかない。
questions.ja: 旅行の前に、ケンジは浜辺の近くの小さなホテルで（　）をした。3泊分の部屋を確実に取っておきたかったのだ。

questions.q: Our science teacher asked us to ____ the plants every morning and write down how tall they had grown since the day before.
questions.why: measure＝「測る」。「どれだけ背が伸びたか書き留める」とあるので、高さを測る。invite（招く）、borrow（借りる）、repeat（くり返す）は植物の高さと合わない。
questions.ja: 理科の先生は私たちに、毎朝植物を（　）、前の日からどれだけ伸びたかを書き留めるように言った。

questions.q: The gift shop at the station sells ____ goods made by artists who live in the town, such as cups, bags, and scarves.
questions.why: local＝「地元の」。町に住む芸術家が作った品、という説明と合う。nervous（緊張した）、rapid（速い）、empty（空の）は品物を説明しない。
questions.ja: 駅の土産物店では、カップやバッグ、スカーフなど、町に住む芸術家が作った（　）品物を売っている。

questions.q: Mr. Kim ____ the students to bring their own water bottles on the hiking trip because there would be no stores on the mountain.
questions.why: remind 人 to ～＝「人に～することを思い出させる」。山に店が無いので水筒を持ってくるよう念を押した。「人 + to 不定詞」の形を取れるのは remind だけ。
questions.ja: 山には店が無いので、キム先生は生徒たちにハイキングに自分の水筒を持ってくるよう（　）。

questions.q: Our town's history museum has a large collection of old ____, such as coins, toys, and clocks. Some of them are more than 200 years old.
questions.why: object＝「物・品物」。硬貨・おもちゃ・時計という例から、物が入る。customers（客）、seasons（季節）、languages（言語）は博物館の収集品の例と合わない。
questions.ja: 私たちの町の歴史博物館には、硬貨やおもちゃ、時計など、古い（　）がたくさん集められている。200年以上前の物もある。

questions.q: Tom felt very ____ before his piano recital, but once he started playing, he forgot about the audience and enjoyed himself.
questions.why: nervous＝「緊張した」。but 以下の「弾き始めると観客のことを忘れて楽しんだ」と対比になる。honest（正直な）、modern（現代の）、ancient（古代の）は対比にならない。
questions.ja: トムはピアノの発表会の前にとても（　）が、弾き始めると観客のことを忘れて楽しんだ。

questions.q: This train is very ____ during the morning rush hour. Many passengers cannot find a seat and have to stand all the way to the city.
questions.why: crowded＝「混んでいる」。座れずに立ったままの乗客が多い、という2文目から分かる。silent（静かな）、cheerful（陽気な）、delicious（おいしい）は合わない。
questions.ja: この電車は朝のラッシュアワーにとても（　）。多くの乗客が座れず、都心までずっと立っていなければならない。

questions.q: Sarah wants to become a vet. She volunteers at an animal ____ every weekend, where she feeds dogs and cats that have no homes.
questions.why: animal shelter＝「動物保護施設」。飼い主のいない犬や猫にえさをあげる場所。factory（工場）、stadium（競技場）、airport（空港）は合わない。
questions.ja: サラは獣医になりたいと思っている。彼女は毎週末、動物（　）でボランティアをして、家の無い犬や猫にえさをあげている。

questions.q: The city has started a new program to ____ plastic bottles. People put them in blue boxes, and the bottles are made into clothes and bags.
questions.why: recycle＝「リサイクルする」。ペットボトルが服やバッグに作り変えられる、という説明と合う。decorate（飾る）、translate（翻訳する）、celebrate（祝う）は合わない。
questions.ja: 市はペットボトルを（　）新しい取り組みを始めた。人々が青い箱に入れると、ボトルは服やバッグに作り変えられる。

questions.q: When Jack's new computer stopped working, he took it back to the store. The staff agreed to ____ it because he had bought it only a week before.
questions.why: replace＝「取り替える」。買って1週間なので新品と交換してくれた。repeat（くり返す）、refuse（断る）、respect（尊敬する）は、agreed to（同意した）や理由と合わない。形の似た語に注意。
questions.ja: ジャックの新しいコンピューターが動かなくなったので、彼はそれを店に持って行った。買ってまだ1週間だったので、店員は（　）ことに同意した。

questions.q: Lily felt ____ after her best friend moved to another city. To feel better, she joined the school drama club and made some new friends.
questions.why: lonely＝「さびしい」。親友が引っ越した後の気持ちで、新しい友達を作って元気になった、という流れ。brave（勇敢な）、famous（有名な）、careful（注意深い）は合わない。
questions.ja: リリーは親友が別の町へ引っ越した後、（　）と感じた。元気を出すため、彼女は学校の演劇部に入り、新しい友達を作った。

questions.q: The pilot told the ____ that the plane would arrive at the airport twenty minutes early because of strong winds from behind.
questions.why: passenger＝「乗客」。パイロットが到着時刻を伝える相手は乗客。patients（患者）、neighbors（近所の人）、audiences（観客）は飛行機の場面と合わない。
questions.ja: 後ろからの強い風のおかげで、飛行機は空港に20分早く着くとパイロットは（　）に伝えた。

questions.q: Ms. Lee gave her students a ____ for their history reports. They have to hand them in by next Friday at the latest.
questions.why: deadline＝「締め切り」。「遅くとも来週金曜までに提出」が締め切りの内容。prize（賞）、rumor（うわさ）、habit（習慣）は合わない。
questions.ja: リー先生は生徒たちに歴史のレポートの（　）を伝えた。遅くとも来週の金曜日までに提出しなければならない。

questions.q: Takeshi is trying hard to ____ his English. He reads an English news website every morning and watches movies without Japanese subtitles.
questions.why: improve＝「上達させる」。毎朝英語のニュースを読み、字幕なしで映画を見るのは英語を伸ばすため。explain（説明する）、complain（不平を言う）、imagine（想像する）は合わない。
questions.ja: タケシは英語を（　）ために一生懸命がんばっている。毎朝英語のニュースサイトを読み、日本語字幕なしで映画を見ている。

questions.q: The zoo ____ a lot of visitors last month when a baby panda was shown to the public for the first time.
questions.why: attract＝「（人を）引きつける」。赤ちゃんパンダの初公開で客が大勢来た。rescued（救助した）、borrowed（借りた）、compared（比べた）は visitors と合わない。
questions.ja: 先月、赤ちゃんパンダが初めて公開された時、その動物園は多くの来園者を（　）。

questions.q: Many people visit the forest to see its rare birds. Volunteers work hard to ____ the birds' nests from people who walk too close.
questions.why: protect A from B＝「BからAを守る」。近づきすぎる人から巣を守る。from と結びつくのは protect。deliver（配達する）、invent（発明する）、pretend（ふりをする）は合わない。
questions.ja: 多くの人が珍しい鳥を見にその森を訪れる。ボランティアたちは、近づきすぎる人から鳥の巣を（　）ために懸命に働いている。

questions.q: This soup has many healthy ____, such as carrots, beans, and onions. It is also cheap and easy to make at home.
questions.why: ingredient＝「材料」。ニンジン・豆・タマネギはスープの材料。instruments（楽器・器具）、seasons（季節）、reasons（理由）は例と合わない。
questions.ja: このスープにはニンジンや豆、タマネギなど、体に良い（　）がたくさん入っている。安くて家で簡単に作れもする。

questions.q: Daniel has a dentist's ____ at three o'clock this afternoon, so he has to leave school early today.
questions.why: appointment＝「（病院などの）予約・約束」。3時に歯医者の予約があるので早退する。experiment（実験）、environment（環境）、advertisement（広告）は語尾が似ているだけ。
questions.ja: ダニエルは今日の午後3時に歯医者の（　）があるので、学校を早退しなければならない。

questions.q: The weather report says that the ____ will drop below zero tonight, so you should wear a warm coat if you go out.
questions.why: temperature＝「気温」。below zero（0度より下）に下がるのは気温。population（人口）、atmosphere（雰囲気・大気）、distance（距離）は合わない。
questions.ja: 天気予報によると今夜は（　）が0度より下がるので、出かけるなら暖かいコートを着たほうがいい。

questions.q: Many tourists buy ____ such as key chains and postcards at the shop near the castle. They give them to their friends back home.
questions.why: souvenir＝「お土産・記念品」。観光客が買って友達にあげるキーホルダーや絵はがき。symbols（象徴）、engines（エンジン）、lessons（授業）は合わない。
questions.ja: 多くの観光客が城の近くの店でキーホルダーや絵はがきなどの（　）を買う。彼らはそれを地元の友達にあげるのだ。

questions.q: Kate loves nature. During her summer vacation, she plans to ____ the forests and lakes of northern Canada with a tour guide.
questions.why: explore＝「探検する・見て回る」。自然好きのケイトがガイドと森や湖を回る。obey（従う）、ignore（無視する）、divide（分ける）は合わない。
questions.ja: ケイトは自然が大好きだ。夏休みに、彼女はツアーガイドと一緒にカナダ北部の森や湖を（　）予定だ。

questions.q: Living near the station is very ____ for Maria. She can walk there in three minutes and get to her office quickly.
questions.why: convenient＝「便利な」。駅まで歩いて3分で、すぐに会社に着ける。terrible（ひどい）、patient（がまん強い）、ancient（古代の）は2文目と合わない。
questions.ja: 駅の近くに住むのはマリアにとってとても（　）。駅まで歩いて3分で、会社にすぐ着ける。

questions.q: After hiking for six hours, everyone was ____. They lay down on the grass and rested for an hour before eating lunch.
questions.why: exhausted＝「へとへとに疲れた」。6時間歩いて、草の上に寝転んで休んだ、という流れ。curious（好奇心の強い）、polite（礼儀正しい）、similar（似ている）は合わない。
questions.ja: 6時間ハイキングした後、みんな（　）。昼食を食べる前に草の上に寝転んで1時間休んだ。

questions.q: The teacher asked Yuki to ____ a short Japanese poem into English for the international students in her class.
questions.why: translate A into B＝「AをBに翻訳する」。日本語の詩を英語にする。pronounce（発音する）、exchange（交換する）、describe（説明する）は into English の形と合わない。
questions.ja: 先生はユキに、クラスの留学生のために日本語の短い詩を英語に（　）ように頼んだ。

questions.q: Ryan ____ his parents' wedding anniversary by cooking a special dinner for them. He made pasta and a chocolate cake.
questions.why: celebrate＝「祝う」。結婚記念日に特別な夕食を作った。repaired（修理した）、predicted（予想した）、wasted（むだにした）は記念日と合わない。
questions.ja: ライアンは両親の結婚記念日を、特別な夕食を作って（　）。彼はパスタとチョコレートケーキを作った。

questions.q: Amy's little brother was sick in bed, so she had to stay home and ____ him while her parents were at work.
questions.why: look after ～＝「～の世話をする」。両親が仕事の間、病気の弟の面倒を見た。look up（調べる）、put on（着る）、give up（あきらめる）は合わない。
questions.ja: エイミーの弟は病気で寝ていたので、両親が仕事の間、彼女は家にいて弟（　）なければならなかった。

questions.q: Kevin ____ his old math teacher at the airport yesterday. They had not seen each other for more than ten years.
questions.why: run into ～＝「～に偶然会う」。10年以上会っていなかった先生と空港で会った。turned down（断った）、took off（脱いだ・離陸した）、called back（折り返し電話した）は合わない。
questions.ja: ケビンは昨日、空港で昔の数学の先生に（　）。2人は10年以上会っていなかった。

questions.q: If you want to join the cooking class, please sign up ____. We need to know the number of students one week before the class.
questions.why: in advance＝「前もって」。1週間前に人数を知る必要がある、という2文目と合う。by heart（暗記して）、on foot（歩いて）、in public（人前で）は合わない。
questions.ja: 料理教室に参加したい場合は、（　）申し込んでください。教室の1週間前に生徒の人数を知る必要があります。

questions.q: Jenny was ____ of spiders when she was a child, but now she keeps one as a pet in her room.
questions.why: be afraid of ～＝「～をこわがる」。but 以下の「今はペットとして飼っている」と対比になる。fond of（好き）では but の対比にならない。proud of（誇りに思う）、full of（いっぱい）も合わない。
questions.ja: ジェニーは子どものころクモが（　）が、今は自分の部屋でペットとして1匹飼っている。

questions.q: The soccer game was ____ because of the heavy snow. The two teams will play the game next Sunday instead.
questions.why: call off ～＝「～を中止する」（受け身で was called off）。大雪で中止になり、来週代わりに行う。put away（片付ける）、hand in（提出する）、show up（現れる）は合わない。
questions.ja: 大雪のため、そのサッカーの試合は（　）。2チームは代わりに来週の日曜日に試合をする予定だ。

questions.q: Tim has been ____ to the summer festival for weeks. He has already decided which food stalls he will visit.
questions.why: look forward to ～＝「～を楽しみにする」。何週間も前から屋台を決めている。get along（うまくやる）、run out（なくなる）、take part（参加する）は後ろに to を取れない（take part は in）。
questions.ja: ティムは何週間も前から夏祭りを（　）いる。どの屋台に行くかもう決めている。

questions.q: Please ____ this form with your name and address, and then give it to the woman at the front desk.
questions.why: fill out ～＝「（用紙）に記入する」。名前と住所を書いて受付に渡す。cut down（切り倒す・減らす）、break down（故障する）、grow up（成長する）は合わない。
questions.ja: この用紙に名前と住所を（　）、受付の女性に渡してください。

questions.q: Mr. Davis told his students to ____ their phones during the test. If a phone rings, the student will have to leave the room.
questions.why: turn off ～＝「（電源）を切る」。電話が鳴ったら退室、という2文目と合う。set up（設置する）、bring up（育てる・話題に出す）、make up（作り上げる）は合わない。
questions.ja: デイビス先生は生徒たちに、テストの間は電話の電源を（　）ように言った。電話が鳴ったら、その生徒は部屋を出なければならない。

questions.q:
A: Have you ever ____ to Kyoto, Amanda?
B: Yes, I went there with my family two years ago. We visited many old temples.
questions.why: have been to ～＝「～に行ったことがある」（現在完了・経験）。Have の後ろは過去分詞なので been。go・going・went は have の後ろに置けない。
questions.ja: A：アマンダ、京都に（　）ことはある？　B：ええ、2年前に家族と行ったわ。古いお寺をたくさん訪れたの。

questions.q: The girl ____ is talking with Mr. Brown is a new student from Australia. Her name is Chloe, and she likes surfing.
questions.why: 先行詞 The girl（人）で、後ろに主語が欠けた is talking が続くので、主格の関係代名詞 who。which は物、whose は後ろに名詞が要る、what は先行詞を取らない。
questions.ja: ブラウン先生と話している女の子（　）は、オーストラリアから来た新入生だ。名前はクロエで、サーフィンが好きだ。

questions.q: If I ____ more free time, I would join the school band. But I have to study for my exams every day.
questions.why: 仮定法過去：If + 主語 + 過去形, 主語 + would + 動詞の原形。後半の I would join と「でも毎日勉強しなければならない」から、現実と違う仮定。
questions.ja: もし私にもっと自由な時間（　）、学校のバンドに入るのに。でも毎日試験勉強をしなければならない。

questions.q: Ted's mother made him ____ his room before he went out to play soccer with his friends.
questions.why: make + 人 + 動詞の原形＝「人に～させる」（使役）。to clean は make の後ろには使わない（ask や tell なら to 不定詞）。
questions.ja: テッドの母親は、テッドが友達とサッカーをしに出かける前に、彼に部屋を（　）させた。

questions.q: This stone bridge ____ about 100 years ago. It is one of the oldest bridges in the city, and many tourists take pictures of it.
questions.why: 橋は「建てられた」側なので受け身。about 100 years ago（過去の一時点）があるので過去形の受け身 was built。has built は能動で、ago と一緒に使えない。
questions.ja: この石の橋は約100年前に（　）。市内で最も古い橋の1つで、多くの観光客が写真を撮る。

questions.q: Linda is really looking forward to ____ her cousins in Canada during the summer vacation. She has not seen them for three years.
questions.why: look forward to の to は前置詞なので、後ろは動名詞（～ing）。to see としないのがポイント。
questions.ja: リンダは夏休みにカナダのいとこたちに（　）のをとても楽しみにしている。3年間会っていないのだ。

questions.q: Our flight was ____ for two hours because of thick fog, so we had lunch and read magazines at the airport.
questions.why: delayed＝「遅れた」。霧のせいで2時間、空港で昼食をとって待った、という流れに合う。admired（感心された）、wrapped（包まれた）、invented（発明された）は飛行機の便に合わない。
questions.ja: 私たちの飛行機は濃い霧のために2時間（　）ので、空港で昼食を食べたり雑誌を読んだりした。

questions.q: Nora ____ her mother's advice and took an umbrella to school. In the afternoon, it started to rain heavily, so she was glad she did.
questions.why: follow one's advice＝「助言に従う」。母の助言どおり傘を持って行ったので、雨が降って良かったと思った。reduced（減らした）、hired（雇った）、folded（たたんだ）は advice と結びつかない。
questions.ja: ノラは母親の助言に（　）、学校に傘を持って行った。午後に雨が激しく降り出したので、そうして良かったと思った。

questions.q: This old house needs a lot of ____. The roof leaks when it rains, and some of the windows are broken.
questions.why: repair＝「修理」。雨もりがして窓も割れている、という2文目から、修理が必要だと分かる。rumors（うわさ）、flavors（味）、fashions（流行）は家に必要な物ではない。
questions.ja: この古い家はたくさんの（　）が必要だ。雨が降ると屋根から水がもれるし、窓もいくつか割れている。

questions.q: Ms. Harper is very ____. She often buys lunch for the people she works with, and she gave all her old books to the town library.
questions.why: generous＝「気前のよい」。同僚に昼食をおごり、本を図書館に寄付する、という行動と合う。strict（厳しい）、jealous（嫉妬深い）、dull（退屈な）は2文目と合わない。
questions.ja: ハーパーさんはとても（　）。一緒に働く人たちによく昼食をおごり、古い本を全部町の図書館にあげた。

questions.q: The museum does not ____ visitors to take pictures inside, so please put your cameras away before you enter.
questions.why: allow ～ to ...＝「～が…するのを許す」。カメラをしまうように、という後半から、館内の撮影は許されていない。lend（貸す）、pour（注ぐ）は意味が合わず、suggest は ～ to ... の形をとらない。
questions.ja: その博物館は来館者が館内で写真を撮ることを（　）ので、入る前にカメラをしまってください。

questions.q: Kyle's ____ is to become a professional chef. He practices cooking every day and plans to study in Italy after high school.
questions.why: goal＝「目標」。プロの料理人になるために毎日練習している、という2文目と合う。matter（問題）、voice（声）、fact（事実）は「～になること」の主語として合わない。
questions.ja: カイルの（　）はプロの料理人になることだ。毎日料理の練習をしていて、高校を出たらイタリアで学ぶつもりだ。

questions.q: The students were deeply ____ by the old man's story about his life in the village. Some of them even cried.
questions.why: be moved＝「感動する」。泣いた生徒もいた、という2文目から、話に心を動かされたと分かる。bored（退屈した）では泣いた理由にならない。
questions.ja: 生徒たちは、村での暮らしについてのおじいさんの話に深く（　）。泣いている生徒さえいた。

questions.q: Please be ____ when you walk on this floor. It has just been cleaned, and it is still wet.
questions.why: careful＝「気をつける」。床がまだぬれているので、歩く時に注意して、という意味。active（活発な）、wealthy（裕福な）、rude（失礼な）はぬれた床の注意にならない。
questions.ja: この床を歩く時は（　）ください。掃除したばかりで、まだぬれています。

questions.q: Mr. Ford ____ a small bakery in the town. He gets up at four every morning to bake bread for his customers.
questions.why: run＝「（店などを）経営する」。毎朝4時に起きて客のためにパンを焼く、という2文目と合う。rides（乗る）、spends（費やす）、wins（勝つ）はパン屋と結びつかない。
questions.ja: フォードさんは町で小さなパン屋を（　）。毎朝4時に起きて、お客さんのためにパンを焼く。

questions.q: Students need to get ____ from their teacher before they use the computers in the science room.
questions.why: permission＝「許可」。コンピューターを使う前に先生から許可をもらう必要がある。pollution（汚染）、invention（発明）、emotion（感情）は get ～ from their teacher と合わない。
questions.ja: 生徒は、理科室のコンピューターを使う前に先生から（　）をもらう必要がある。

questions.q: The camping store rents all the ____ you need for your trip, such as tents, sleeping bags, and cooking pots.
questions.why: equipment＝「道具・用具」。テント・寝袋・なべ、という例から、キャンプの道具だと分かる。weather（天気）、scenery（景色）、behavior（ふるまい）は貸し出せない。
questions.ja: そのキャンプ用品店では、テントや寝袋、料理用のなべなど、旅行に必要な（　）を全部貸してくれる。

questions.q: Doctors say that washing your hands well before you eat can help ____ colds and other illnesses.
questions.why: prevent＝「防ぐ」。食事の前によく手を洗うことは、かぜなどの病気を防ぐのに役立つ。require（必要とする）、observe（観察する）、attend（出席する）は意味が合わない。
questions.ja: 医者によると、食べる前に手をよく洗うことは、かぜやほかの病気を（　）のに役立つ。

questions.q: This old watch is very ____. It belonged to my great-grandfather, and it is worth a lot of money now.
questions.why: valuable＝「価値のある・高価な」。今では大金の価値がある、という2文目と合う。ordinary（ふつうの）は逆の意味。noisy（うるさい）、shy（内気な）は合わない。
questions.ja: この古い腕時計はとても（　）。ひいおじいさんの物で、今ではとても高い値打ちがある。

questions.q: In the class discussion, the teacher asked the students to share their ____ about school lunches. Most of them said they wanted more fruit.
questions.why: opinion＝「意見」。話し合いで給食についての考えを言い、多くが「果物を増やしてほしい」と言った。accidents（事故）、materials（材料）、harvests（収穫）は share ～ about school lunches に合わない。
questions.ja: クラスの話し合いで、先生は生徒たちに給食についての（　）を出し合うように言った。ほとんどの生徒が果物を増やしてほしいと言った。

questions.q: Ben could not ____ the last math problem on the test, so he asked his teacher how to do it after class.
questions.why: solve＝「（問題を）解く」。最後の数学の問題が解けなかったので、先生にやり方を聞いた。rescue（救う）、gather（集める）、predict（予想する）は問題を解く意味にならない。
questions.ja: ベンはテストの最後の数学の問題を（　）ので、授業の後で先生に解き方を聞いた。

questions.q: I ____ tea to coffee. Coffee is too bitter for me, so I usually drink green tea in the morning.
questions.why: prefer A to B＝「BよりAが好き」。コーヒーは苦すぎるので朝は緑茶、という2文目と合う。compare A to B（比べる）は形は合うが、好みを表さない。
questions.ja: 私はコーヒーより紅茶が（　）。コーヒーは私には苦すぎるので、朝はたいてい緑茶を飲む。

questions.q: Mei won first prize in a singing ____ last month. More than fifty people took part, and she was the youngest of them all.
questions.why: competition＝「大会・コンテスト」。1位を取り、50人以上が参加した、という内容と合う。condition（状態）、location（場所）、operation（手術・操作）では1位を取れない。
questions.ja: メイは先月、歌の（　）で1位を取った。50人以上が参加し、その中で彼女がいちばん年下だった。

questions.q: When Owen got to the station, he ____ that he had left his wallet at home, so he had to go back to get it.
questions.why: realize＝「気づく」。駅に着いて財布を家に忘れたと気づき、取りに戻った。decided（決めた）や promised（約束した）は「忘れた」という過去の事実と合わない。
questions.ja: オーウェンは駅に着いた時、財布を家に置いてきたことに（　）、取りに戻らなければならなかった。

questions.q: The young man on the bus was very ____. He said "thank you" to the driver and gave his seat to an elderly woman.
questions.why: polite＝「礼儀正しい」。運転手にお礼を言い、お年寄りに席をゆずった、という2文目と合う。lazy（怠けた）、silly（ばかげた）、strange（変な）は合わない。
questions.ja: バスに乗っていたその若い男性はとても（　）。運転手に「ありがとう」と言い、お年寄りの女性に席をゆずった。

questions.q: Our cat ____ for three days, but then she suddenly came home. She was hungry but healthy.
questions.why: disappear＝「いなくなる」。3日後に突然帰ってきた、という but の後と合う。discovered（発見した）、delivered（配達した）は目的語が必要で、decreased（減った）は意味が合わない。
questions.ja: うちの猫は3日間（　）が、突然家に帰ってきた。おなかはすいていたが元気だった。

questions.q: Many ____ animals, such as deer and foxes, live in the forest near our town. People should not give them any food.
questions.why: wild＝「野生の」。森にすむシカやキツネは野生動物で、えさを与えてはいけない。modern（現代の）、plain（質素な）、rude（失礼な）は動物の種類を表さない。
questions.ja: シカやキツネなど、たくさんの（　）動物が町の近くの森にすんでいる。人はそれらにえさをあげてはいけない。

questions.q: Dr. Morgan ____ that I get more sleep and drink more water. She said it would help with my headaches.
questions.why: suggest that ～＝「～するよう勧める」。医者が睡眠と水分をとるよう勧め、頭痛に効くと言った。complained（文句を言った）、guessed（推測した）、refused（断った）は助言の意味にならない。
questions.ja: モーガン先生（医師）は、もっと睡眠をとって水をたくさん飲むように（　）。それで頭痛が良くなるだろうと言った。

questions.q: Studying abroad gives students a good ____ to learn about other cultures and make friends from different countries.
questions.why: opportunity＝「機会」。留学は異文化を学び、外国の友達を作る良い機会になる。emergency（緊急事態）、quantity（量）、signature（署名）は a good ～ to learn と合わない。
questions.ja: 留学は、生徒にほかの文化について学び、いろいろな国の友達を作る良い（　）を与えてくれる。

questions.q: We had to ____ our barbecue until next weekend because the weather report said it would rain all day on Saturday.
questions.why: put off ～ until ...＝「～を…まで延期する」。土曜は1日中雨の予報なので、バーベキューを来週末に延ばした。get over（乗り越える）、pick out（選び出す）、hold on（待つ）は until next weekend と合わない。
questions.ja: 天気予報で土曜日は1日中雨だと言っていたので、私たちはバーベキューを来週末まで（　）なければならなかった。

questions.q: It took Riku two weeks to ____ his bad cold. He stayed in bed and drank a lot of hot tea.
questions.why: get over＝「（病気などから）回復する」。ひどいかぜが治るのに2週間かかった。look into（調べる）、come across（偶然出会う）、hand out（配る）はかぜと合わない。
questions.ja: リクがひどいかぜから（　）のに2週間かかった。ベッドで寝て、温かいお茶をたくさん飲んだ。

questions.q: Ms. Rivera is ____ of the school's English club. She plans all of the club's activities and events.
questions.why: be in charge of ～＝「～の担当・責任者である」。部の活動や行事を全部計画している、という2文目と合う。in front of（～の前に）、in danger of（～の危険がある）は意味が合わない。
questions.ja: リベラ先生は学校の英語部の（　）。部の活動や行事を全部計画している。

questions.q: Ella ____ a great idea for the class party. She suggested that everyone bring a dish from a different country.
questions.why: come up with ～＝「（考えなど）を思いつく」。いろいろな国の料理を持ち寄る、というアイデアを思いついた。got rid of（取り除いた）、ran out of（使い果たした）は great idea と合わない。
questions.ja: エラはクラスのパーティーのためにすばらしいアイデアを（　）。みんながちがう国の料理を1品持ってくることを提案したのだ。

questions.q: ____ the weather news, it will be sunny and warm tomorrow, so let's go to the beach.
questions.why: according to ～＝「～によると」。天気予報によると明日は晴れて暖かいので、海に行こう。Instead of（～の代わりに）、In addition to（～に加えて）、Far from（～から遠い）は情報源を表さない。
questions.ja: 天気予報（　）、明日は晴れて暖かいそうだから、海に行こう。

questions.q: Last month, Mr. Tanaka visited his hometown for the first time ____ ten years. Many things there had changed.
questions.why: for the first time in ～ years＝「～年ぶりに」。10年ぶりに故郷を訪ねたら、いろいろ変わっていた。at・by・on はこの形で使わない。
questions.ja: 先月、タナカさんは10年（　）故郷を訪れた。そこでは多くのことが変わっていた。

questions.q: Could you ____ your little sister at the station at five? She is coming back from her piano lesson.
questions.why: pick up ～＝「～を車などで迎えに行く」。駅で妹を迎えて、という頼み。find out（見つけ出す）、take after（似ている）、stand for（表す）は駅で人に会う意味にならない。
questions.ja: 5時に駅で妹を（　）くれる？ピアノのレッスンから帰ってくるんだ。

questions.q: Noah really ____ his father. They both have curly hair, and they both love telling jokes.
questions.why: take after ～＝「（親）に似ている」。髪も冗談好きなところも父と同じ。looks into（調べる）、gives away（ただであげる）、puts out（消す）は2文目と合わない。
questions.ja: ノアは本当に父親に（　）。2人とも髪がくせ毛で、2人とも冗談を言うのが大好きだ。

questions.q: Maya wanted to visit the art museum with her grandmother, so she used the internet to ____ what time it opens on Sundays.
questions.why: find out＝「（調べて）知る」。インターネットで日曜の開館時間を調べた。show off（見せびらかす）、turn up（現れる）、hang up（電話を切る）は what time ～ を目的語にとらない。
questions.ja: マヤは祖母と美術館に行きたかったので、インターネットを使って日曜日に何時に開くかを（　）。

questions.q: Shota's English is improving ____. At first, he could say only a few words, but now he can talk with his host family.
questions.why: little by little＝「少しずつ」。最初は少しの単語だけ→今は会話できる、と時間をかけて上達している。all at once（突然・一度に）は逆、face to face（向かい合って）は合わない。
questions.ja: ショウタの英語は（　）上達している。最初は少しの単語しか言えなかったが、今はホストファミリーと話ができる。

questions.q: It was so hot yesterday afternoon ____ my friends and I decided to go swimming in the river near our school.
questions.why: so ～ that ...＝「とても～なので…」。とても暑かったので川で泳ぐことにした。前に so があるので that が入る。
questions.ja: 昨日の午後はとても暑かった（　）、友達と私は学校の近くの川へ泳ぎに行くことにした。

questions.q: I have a friend ____ mother works as a pilot. She sometimes tells us interesting stories about flying.
questions.why: 空所の後に mother（名詞）が続き、「その友達の母親」という意味になるので所有格の関係代名詞 whose。who・which の後には動詞などが続く。
questions.ja: 私には、母親がパイロットとして働いている友達がいる。その母親は時々、飛行機の面白い話をしてくれる。

questions.q: Nina ____ in this town since she was five years old, so she knows all the good places to eat.
questions.why: since ～（～から今まで）があるので現在完了 has lived。5歳の時から住んでいるので、いい店を全部知っている。lives・is living は since と使わない。
questions.ja: ニナは5歳の時からこの町に（　）ので、おいしい店を全部知っている。

questions.q: My brother is not old ____ to get a driver's license. He has to wait two more years.
questions.why: ～ enough to ...＝「…するのに十分～」。not old enough で「免許を取れる年齢ではない」。too は too old to ～ の形で old の前に置き、so・very は後ろに to をとらない。
questions.ja: 兄［弟］は運転免許を取れる（　）年齢ではない。あと2年待たなければならない。

questions.q: When the teacher came into the classroom, the students stopped ____ with each other and sat down quietly at their desks.
questions.why: stop ～ing＝「～するのをやめる」。先生が来たのでおしゃべりをやめて静かに座った。stop to talk は「話すために立ち止まる」で、静かに座ったことと合わない。
questions.ja: 先生が教室に入ってくると、生徒たちはおしゃべり（　）、静かに自分の席に座った。

questions.q: Our coach always says that it is important ____ us to drink enough water during practice on hot summer days.
questions.why: It is ～ for 人 to ...＝「人が…するのは～だ」。important のように物事を評価する形容詞の時は for。of は kind・nice など人の性質を表す形容詞の時に使う。
questions.ja: コーチはいつも、暑い夏の日の練習中は、私たち（　）十分な水を飲むことが大切だと言う。

questions.q: Do you know ____ the next bus will come? I've been waiting here for twenty minutes.
questions.why: 「次のバスがいつ来るか知っていますか」という間接疑問。20分待っている、という2文目から時を聞いている。what・who・which では主語や目的語が欠けた文になってしまう。
questions.ja: 次のバスが（　）来るか知っていますか。ここで20分待っているんです。

parts.title: 大問2 会話文の空所補充
parts.desc: 短い会話の空所に入る文や語句を4つから選ぶ
parts.tip: 空所の直後の1行が一番のヒント（Yes / No の答え方、Oh, no! などの反応、Then ～ の判断）。Have you ～? なら have で答える、など質問と答えの形もそろえる。
parts.intro: Read each conversation and choose the best sentence or phrase for the blank.

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. I'd like to buy this jacket, but it's a little too big for me.
B: ( ) We may have the same jacket in a smaller size.
A: Great. Can I try it on?
B: Of course.

choices: Let me check in the back.
questions.why: 直後の「小さいサイズがあるかもしれない」につながるのは「奥で確かめてみます」。値引き・支払い方法・店員が買った話は、サイズの相談に答えていない。

sets.passage:
A: Mom, can I go to Emma's house after school today?
B: Have you finished your homework yet?
A: ( ) I did it during lunch break.
B: All right, then. But be home by six.

questions.why: Have you finished ～? には Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. で答える。直後の「昼休みにやった」から Yes。No, not yet と I'll do it tomorrow はその後の内容と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Dad, I'm thinking of joining the tennis club at school.
B: That sounds great. But don't you need a racket?
A: Yes. ( )
B: Sure. Let's go to the sports shop this weekend.

choices: Could you buy one for me?
questions.why: 父の Sure. Let's go to the sports shop（いいよ、スポーツ店に行こう）は、ラケットを買ってほしいという頼みへの返事。I already have two は Yes（必要）と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Hello, Greenfield Restaurant.
B: Hi. I'd like to book a table for four people this Saturday evening.
A: I'm sorry, but ( ). How about Sunday?
B: Sunday is fine. Seven o'clock, please.

choices: we close at five on weekdays
the table is by the window
questions.why: I'm sorry, but の後に土曜が無理な理由が来て、日曜を勧めている。fully booked＝「予約でいっぱい」。土曜は平日（weekdays）ではないので、平日の閉店時間は理由にならない。

sets.passage:
A: How was your trip to Hawaii, Ken?
B: It was great, but ( ).
A: Oh, no! What did you do?
B: I bought a new one at a shop near my hotel.

choices: the weather was perfect every day
I stayed there for a week
I lost my swimsuit on the first day
questions.why: but の後は良くない出来事。A の Oh, no! と、B の「新しい物を買った」から、何かをなくしたと分かる。ほかの3つは困った話ではない。

sets.passage:
A: Ms. Clark, ( )?
B: Sure. What part don't you understand?
A: This question about the moon. I don't know how to start.
B: OK. Let's look at it together.

choices: when is the next school trip
could you help me with my science homework
may I go home early today
questions.why: 先生の「どこが分からないの？」と、月についての問題、という流れから、宿題を手伝ってほしいという頼み。ほかの質問には What part don't you understand? と返さない。

sets.passage:
A: I'm going to the supermarket now. Do you need anything for tonight's dinner?
B: Yes. ( )
A: OK. Anything else?
B: No, that's all. Thanks a lot, Dad.

choices: Could you get some eggs and milk?
questions.why: Do you need anything? に Yes と答えた後は、買ってきてほしい物を言う。A の Anything else?（ほかには？）もそれを示す。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Does this bus go to the city museum?
B: No, it doesn't. ( )
A: I see. Where can I catch it?
B: At the bus stop across the street.

choices: You need to take the Number 12.
questions.why: A の Where can I catch it?（どこで乗れますか）の it は別のバス。だから空所では乗るべきバスを教えている。I'm going there, too は No, it doesn't と合わない。

sets.passage:
A: Jason, you look tired. Are you OK?
B: ( ) I stayed up late watching a soccer game.
A: You should go to bed earlier tonight.
B: I know.

choices: I didn't get much sleep last night.
I just had a big lunch.
questions.why: 疲れている理由が「サッカーの試合を見て夜ふかしした」なので、あまり眠れなかった、が入る。10時間寝たは矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Welcome to Pine Hill Zoo. How many tickets would you like?
B: Two adults and one child, please. ( )
A: Yes. Children under six can enter for free.
B: Oh, good. My daughter is four.

choices: What time does the zoo close?
Is there a discount for small children?
questions.why: 答えの「6歳未満は無料です」から、子どもの料金について聞いたと分かる。ほかの質問には Children under six ～ と答えない。

sets.passage:
A: Grandma, this apple cake is delicious. ( )
B: Yes. I made it with apples from our garden.
A: Can you teach me how to make it?
B: Of course.

questions.why: Yes. I made it（ええ、私が作ったの）に合う質問は「自分で焼いたの？」。後の「作り方を教えて」にもつながる。

sets.passage:
A: Lisa, are you coming to the beach with us on Sunday?
B: I'd like to, but ( ).
A: That's too bad. Maybe next time, then.
B: Yes. Have fun!

choices: I love swimming in the sea
I have to work at my part-time job
questions.why: I'd like to, but ～（行きたいけど～）の後は行けない理由。A の That's too bad. も断られたことを示す。ほかの3つは行けない理由にならない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. I think there's a mistake on my bill.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. ( )
A: I only had one coffee, but I was charged for two.
B: Let me fix that right away.

choices: What seems to be the problem?
questions.why: 直後に客が何が違うか説明しているので、店員は「どうなさいましたか」と聞いた。デザートやおつりの話には、この説明は続かない。

sets.passage:
A: Hi, Mike. Did you see the new science fiction movie?
B: Not yet. ( )
A: Yes. It was really exciting. You should see it.
B: OK. I'll go this weekend.

questions.why: A が Yes. It was really exciting. と感想を言うので、B は「君は見たの？」と聞き返した。I saw it twice と It was too long は Not yet（まだ）と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Mom, I can't find my blue umbrella anywhere.
B: ( ) You used it yesterday when it was raining.
A: Oh, you're right! It's there. Thanks, Mom.

choices: It's going to be sunny today.
Did you look by the front door?
I don't like the color blue.
questions.why: A の「そうだ！そこにあった」から、母が探す場所を教えたと分かる。ほかの3つは傘のある場所を示していない。

sets.passage:
A: I'm going to the library to study. Do you want to come?
B: ( ) I have a big history test on Monday.
A: Great. Let's meet at the front gate in ten minutes.

questions.why: A の Great. Let's meet ～ から、B は誘いを受けた。月曜にテストがある、も一緒に行く理由。No, I've already finished studying は誘いを断っている。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. How long does it take to get to the airport by taxi?
B: Usually about thirty minutes. ( )
A: Then I'll take the train instead.
B: That's a good idea.

choices: The taxi drivers here are very kind.
But the roads are very busy at this time of day.
questions.why: A が「それなら電車にする」と言うので、タクシーをやめる理由が入る。今の時間は道が混んでいる、が理由になる。ほかの3つはタクシーをやめる理由にならない。

sets.passage:
A: Dad, can we get a dog?
B: ( ) Who will take it for walks every day?
A: I will! I promise I'll walk it every morning before school.
B: Well, let's talk about it with Mom.

choices: Dogs need a lot of care.
questions.why: 後ろの「誰が毎日散歩に連れて行くの？」から、父は犬の世話の大変さを心配している。We already have two dogs は A の頼み方と合わない。

sets.passage:
A: Hello. I'd like to send this package to Canada.
B: Sure. ( )
A: As fast as possible, please. It's a birthday present.
B: Then express mail is best. It will arrive in three days.

choices: How would you like to send it?
Would you like a bag for it?
questions.why: A の As fast as possible（できるだけ速く）と、B の express mail（速達）から、送り方を聞いたと分かる。

sets.passage:
A: Wow, your garden is beautiful, Mrs. Hill!
B: Thank you. ( )
A: Really? That must be a lot of work.
B: Yes, but I enjoy it.

choices: I don't like flowers very much.
My son lives in another city.
I spend two hours working in it every day.
I bought these flowers this morning.
questions.why: A の「それは大変な作業でしょうね」に合うのは、毎日2時間庭仕事をしている、という話。けさ花を買っただけでは大変な作業にならない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Do you know where the post office is?
B: ( ) It's next to the bank on Main Street.
A: Is it far from here?
B: No. You can walk there in five minutes.

choices: I'm going to send a letter.
questions.why: Do you know ～? には Yes, I do. / No, I don't. で答える。直後に場所を教えているので Yes。No, I don't では後の説明と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Hi, Sean. You look tired. ( )
B: I stayed up late to finish my science report.
A: Did you finish it?
B: Yes, finally. I'm going to bed early tonight.

questions.why: B は「理科のレポートを仕上げるために夜ふかしした」と疲れている理由を説明している。だから「どうしたの？」と聞いたと分かる。

sets.passage:
A: Mom, can I use your laptop this evening?
B: Sure, but ( ). I need it for work tomorrow.
A: I will. I just need it to check my homework online.

choices: please give it back by ten
questions.why: but の後は貸す時の条件。「明日仕事で使う」と A の I will（そうする）から、10時までに返して、が入る。you can keep it（あげる）は明日使う話と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Welcome to Sunrise Books. Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm looking for a cookbook for my mother.
A: ( ) They're on the second floor.
B: Thank you. I'll go and look.

choices: We have a lot of those.
questions.why: 直後の「2階にあります」の They は料理の本のこと。だから「たくさんあります」が入る。雑誌しか売っていないなら2階を案内しない。

sets.passage:
A: Haley, do you want to go to the movies on Saturday?
B: I'd love to, but ( ).
A: That's too bad. How about Sunday?
B: Sunday is perfect.

choices: I have to go to my cousin's wedding
I saw the movie last week
the theater is near my house
questions.why: I'd love to, but ～ の後には行けない理由が入る。A の That's too bad（残念）と日曜の提案から、土曜は用事があると分かる。週末ずっと暇なら断らない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. I think there's a mistake on my bill.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. ( )
A: I ordered one coffee, but you charged me for two.
B: Let me fix that right away.

questions.why: 直後で A が「コーヒー1杯なのに2杯分取られた」と間違いの中身を説明している。だから店員は「どこが違いますか」と聞いた。

sets.passage:
A: Dad, ( )?
B: Of course. What's the problem?
A: My bike chain came off, and I can't put it back on.
B: OK. Let me get my tools.

choices: where did you buy my bike
can you help me with something
do you want to go cycling
questions.why: 父の Of course. What's the problem? と、自転車のチェーンが外れた話から、手伝いを頼んだと分かる。サイクリングの誘いには What's the problem? と返さない。

sets.passage:
A: How was your trip to the mountains, Victor?
B: ( ) It rained every day, so we couldn't go hiking.
A: Oh, that's a shame.
B: Yes. Maybe we'll try again in the fall.

questions.why: 直後の「毎日雨でハイキングできなかった」と A の that's a shame（残念）から、あまり良くなかった旅行。wonderful は後の内容と逆。旅行はもう終わっている。

sets.passage:
A: Hello, Greenhill Dental Clinic.
B: Hi. I'd like to make an appointment for next Tuesday. One of my teeth hurts.
A: ( ) How about Wednesday at two?
B: That's fine. Thank you.

choices: I'm sorry, but we're closed on Tuesdays.
questions.why: A がすぐ水曜日を提案しているので、火曜日は無理という内容が入る。火曜の10時が空いているなら別の日を勧めない。

sets.passage:
A: This curry is delicious, Grandma. ( )
B: Of course. Here you are.
A: Thank you. Did you use a lot of vegetables?
B: Yes. They're from my garden.

questions.why: B が Of course. Here you are.（どうぞ）と何かを渡しているので、おかわりを頼んだと分かる。I'm full（おなかいっぱい）なら渡さない。

sets.passage:
A: Are you going to join the school's sports day, Tyler?
B: Yes. I'm going to run in the relay race.
A: Wow! ( )
B: I practice every day after school.

choices: You must be a fast runner.
questions.why: リレーに出る、と聞いて「足が速いんだね」と言い、B が毎日練習している、と続く。まだ大会前なので「負けたの？」は合わない。

sets.passage:
A: I'd like to buy two tickets for the concert tonight.
B: I'm sorry. ( )
A: Oh, no. Are there any for tomorrow's concert?
B: Yes, we have some seats left.

choices: You can pay by credit card.
questions.why: A の Oh, no と「明日の分はある？」から、今夜のチケットは売り切れ。I'm sorry の後なので困る内容が入る。

sets.passage:
A: Ms. Carter, I'm sorry I'm late. ( )
B: That's OK. But please try to leave home earlier next time.
A: I will. It won't happen again.

choices: My train stopped for twenty minutes.
questions.why: 遅れた言い訳が入る。先生の「次はもっと早く家を出て」と合うのは電車が止まった理由。早く来た・学校の近くに住む、は遅刻の説明にならない。

sets.passage:
A: Do you want to eat out tonight?
B: ( ) I'm too tired to cook.
A: Great. How about the new Italian restaurant on Pine Street?
B: Sounds good.

questions.why: B は「疲れて料理できない」と言い、A が Great と続けているので外食に賛成した。No, let's eat at home は直後の理由と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Is this the right bus for City Hospital?
B: No, ( ). You need to take the Number 7.
A: Where can I catch it?
B: At the stop across the street.

choices: this one goes to the airport
questions.why: No の後に「7番に乗る必要がある」と続くので、このバスは病院に行かない、という内容が入る。歩いて行けるならバスを案内しない。

sets.passage:
A: I can't find my keys anywhere. I have to leave for work in ten minutes.
B: ( )
A: Yes, I looked there twice.
B: Then maybe you left them at the office yesterday.

choices: Did you check your coat pocket?
questions.why: A の「そこは2回見た」という答えから、B は探す場所を聞いた。Yes で答えられる Did you check ～? が合う。

sets.passage:
A: Hi, Megan. I heard you're moving to Osaka next month.
B: That's right. ( )
A: That's great news. I'll miss you, though.
B: I'll miss you, too.

choices: My father got a new job there.
questions.why: 引っ越しの理由が入り、A が That's great news と喜んでいる。父の新しい仕事は良い知らせになる。I'm staying here は引っ越しと矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm looking for a pair of running shoes. I'm going to run in a race next month.
A: ( )
B: Size nine, please.

choices: How much do you want to spend?
questions.why: 直後の答えが Size nine（9号）なので、サイズを聞いたと分かる。色や予算の質問にはサイズでは答えない。

sets.passage:
A: Are you ready for the English test tomorrow, Nanami?
B: Not really. ( )
A: Why don't we study together after school?
B: That would be great.

choices: I don't understand the grammar part.
questions.why: Not really（あまり）と、A が一緒に勉強しようと誘う流れから、困っている内容が入る。週末ずっと勉強した、では一緒に勉強する理由にならない。テストは明日。

sets.passage:
A: Daichi, have you ever been abroad?
B: Yes. ( )
A: Really? What did you do there?
B: I visited a lot of museums and ate a lot of good food.

choices: I went to Spain last year.
I want to go next year.
questions.why: Have you ever been abroad? に Yes と答え、A がそこで何をしたか聞いているので、行った国の話が入る。行きたい・パスポートが無い、では Yes と合わない。

sets.passage:
A: Hello. I'd like to rent a bicycle for the day.
B: Sure. ( )
A: Can I return it after six?
B: I'm afraid not. We close at six.

choices: It's fifteen dollars, and you need to bring it back by six.
questions.why: A が「6時より後に返せるか」と聞いているので、店員は6時までに返すように言ったはず。自転車を貸さないなら Sure と言わない。

sets.passage:
A: Mom, I'm going to Holly's house to study.
B: OK. ( )
A: Around seven. Her mother said she will drive me home.
B: All right. Don't forget to take your umbrella.

choices: How do you go to school?
What time will you be back?
questions.why: 直後の答えが Around seven（7時ごろ）と帰り方なので、何時に戻るかを聞いた。What are you studying? には時刻で答えない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. This jacket looks nice. Can I try it on?
B: Of course. ( )
A: Thanks. I'll be right back.
B: Take your time.

choices: The fitting room is over there.
questions.why: 試着してもいいかと聞かれ、Of course の後は試着室の案内。A は Thanks. I'll be right back と行っている。売り物でないなら Of course と言わない。

sets.passage:
A: What are you going to do this summer vacation, Ren?
B: ( ) I'm going to work at my uncle's farm.
A: That sounds like hard work.
B: Yes, but I love animals.

choices: I'll stay in bed all day.
I don't have any plans yet.
questions.why: 直後におじの農場で働く予定を話しているので、忙しくなる、という内容。予定がまだ無い・1日中寝ている、は後の説明と矛盾し、I went は過去なので合わない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Could you take a picture of us in front of the fountain?
B: Sure. ( )
A: Just press this button on the top.
B: OK. Everyone, smile!

choices: How do I use your camera?
questions.why: A の「このボタンを押すだけ」という答えから、カメラの使い方を聞いたと分かる。出身や初めての訪問かの質問には合わない。

sets.passage:
A: The weather is really nice today. ( )
B: Good idea. Let's take some sandwiches and fruit.
A: I'll make them. You can get the drinks.
B: OK.

choices: Why don't we have a picnic in the park?
Let's stay home and watch TV.
questions.why: B が Good idea. Let's take some sandwiches と答えているので、外で食べる誘い。家でテレビを見るならサンドイッチを持って行かない。

sets.passage:
A: How long have you been learning the piano, Clara?
B: ( )
A: Wow, that's a long time. You must be very good.
B: Well, I still have a lot to learn.

questions.why: How long ～? は期間を聞く。A の that's a long time から「約10年」。Since last month（先月から）では長い時間にならない。Every Saturday は回数。

sets.passage:
A: Hello. This is Wes. May I speak to Paige?
B: I'm sorry, but she's out right now. ( )
A: Yes, please. Could you ask her to call me back?
B: Sure.

questions.why: A の Yes, please. Could you ask her to call me back? は伝言を頼む言い方。だから「伝言を承りましょうか」が入る。A はもう名乗っている。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. ( )
B: Yes. Go straight and turn left at the second corner.
A: Is it far?
B: No, it's only about three minutes from here.

choices: How much is a train ticket?
What time does the station open?
Could you tell me the way to the station?
questions.why: B が道順を説明しているので、駅への行き方を聞いた。開く時間や切符の値段には道順で答えない。

sets.passage:
A: I bought this sweater yesterday, but ( ).
B: I see. Would you like to exchange it for another color?
A: Yes, please. Do you have it in gray?

choices: my sister has the same one
I want to wear it today
questions.why: 店員がほかの色との交換を勧めている。姉［妹］が同じ物を持っているので交換したい、が合う。お気に入りの色・ぴったり合うなら交換しない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Do you know any good places to eat around here?
B: ( ) There's a great noodle shop near the station. It's very popular.
A: Thanks. I'll try it.

questions.why: B は直後に駅近くのラーメン屋を勧めているので、知っている＝Sure。No, sorry. は後の説明と矛盾する。

sets.passage:
A: Kyle, ( ).
B: Thanks, Mom. I studied really hard for it every night.
A: Your father and I are very proud of you. Let's go out for dinner to celebrate.
B: Great!

choices: I heard you passed the exam
questions.why: B が Thanks と「一生懸命勉強した」と言い、母がお祝いの夕食に誘っている。だから試験に合格した話。部屋が散らかっている・お弁当を忘れた、では Thanks と言わない。

sets.passage:
A: Mr. Price, can I ask you about tomorrow's field trip?
B: Sure. What do you want to know?
A: ( )
B: Yes. There are no restaurants near the farm.

choices: Who is going on the trip?
Do we need to bring our own lunch?
questions.why: 先生の答え「はい。農場の近くにはレストランが無い」から、お弁当を持っていく必要があるか聞いた。Who ～? には Yes で答えられない。

sets.passage:
A: Your English is really good, Erika.
B: Thank you. ( )
A: That's why you speak so well.
B: I also watch English movies every weekend.

choices: I lived in Canada for three years.
questions.why: A の That's why ～（だから上手なんだ）の前には上手な理由が入る。カナダに3年住んでいた、が理由になる。英語を勉強しない・難しい、は理由にならない。

sets.passage:
A: Would you like something to drink, Fiona?
B: ( ) Do you have any orange juice?
A: Sorry, we only have apple juice.
B: That's fine, too.

questions.why: 直後に「オレンジジュースはある？」と飲み物を頼んでいるので Yes, please. が入る。No, thanks などは断りなので後と合わない。

sets.passage:
A: I'm thinking of getting a new phone this weekend.
B: ( )
A: The battery doesn't last very long anymore.
B: I see. Then maybe you should get a new one.

choices: Do you like your new phone?
How many phones do you have?
What's wrong with your old one?
questions.why: A は「バッテリーがもう長くもたない」と古い電話の問題を答えている。だから「今のはどうしたの？」と聞いた。まだ新しい電話は買っていない。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. Is this seat taken?
B: No, ( ).
A: Thanks. This train is really crowded today.
B: Yes. There's a baseball game at the stadium.

questions.why: Is this seat taken?（この席はふさがっていますか）に No（空いている）と答えているので、座ってください、が入る。友達が座る・座れないは No と合わない。

sets.passage:
A: What did you think of the movie?
B: ( ) I almost fell asleep.
A: Really? I thought it was exciting.
B: Maybe I was just tired.

choices: I want to see it again.
It was the best movie ever.
questions.why: 直後の「ほとんど寝そうになった」と A の Really? I thought it was exciting（私はわくわくした）から、B はつまらなかった。ほかの3つは楽しんだ感想。

sets.passage:
A: Excuse me. ( ) I want to buy a birthday present for my nephew.
B: It's on the third floor, next to the elevator.
A: Thank you very much.

questions.why: B は「3階のエレベーターの隣」と場所を答えているので、売り場の場所を聞いた。How much ～? には値段で答える。

sets.passage:
A: Grandpa, ( )?
B: I'd love some help. Could you carry these boxes to the garage?
A: Sure. Are they heavy?
B: A little, so be careful.

choices: is there anything I can do for you
what are you doing this weekend
do you want to go out
questions.why: 祖父の I'd love some help（手伝ってくれるとうれしい）から、手伝えることはあるか聞いた。ガレージの場所を聞いたなら箱を運ぶ頼みにはならない。

parts.title: 大問3 長文の語句空所補充（物語）
parts.desc: 約155語の物語文を読み、空所2つに入る語句を4つから選ぶ
parts.tip: 空所の文だけで選ばず、すぐ後ろの1〜2文を読む。物語は「困ったこと → どうしたか → 結果」の順に進むので、空所がどの段階かを考える。つなぎ語の空所は前後が逆の内容なら However。
parts.intro: Read the story and choose the best word or phrase for each numbered blank.

sets.passage:
The Garden Club

Rina is a high school student. Last spring, her teacher, Mr. Ito, started a garden club at her school. Rina was not very interested in plants, but her best friend, Aya, wanted to join. Aya did not want to go to the meetings alone, so she asked Rina to come with her. Rina decided to ( 1 ). At the first meeting, the members planted tomatoes, beans, and sunflowers behind the gym.

At first, Rina thought the work was boring. However, when she saw the first small tomatoes in June, she was very excited. She began to visit the garden every morning before class to water the plants. By August, the club had grown a lot of vegetables. Mr. Ito suggested ( 2 ). The members made tomato soup and bean salad and served them to visitors at the school festival. Many people said the food was delicious. Now, Rina wants to grow vegetables at home, too.

questions.why: アヤが一人で行きたくないので一緒に来てと頼み、直後に「最初の集まりで部員たちが植えた」と続く。だからリナは一緒に入部した。quit（やめる）や別の部を作る、では後の話とつながらない。

choices: selling them at a local market
using them to make dishes for the festival
taking them home to their families
questions.why: 空所の後に「部員はトマトスープと豆のサラダを作り、学園祭で出した」とある。先生の提案は野菜で料理を作ること。市場で売る・家に持ち帰るは、後の文と合わない。

sets.passage:
A Dog Named Pepper

Last year, Daniel's family got a dog from an animal shelter. They named her Pepper. She loved playing with Daniel's little sister in the yard. Pepper was friendly, but she had one problem. Whenever someone rang the doorbell, she barked loudly for several minutes. Daniel's neighbors were not happy about the noise, so his parents told him to ( 1 ).

Daniel read some books about training dogs. One book said that dogs learn best when they get a reward. So every time the doorbell rang and Pepper stayed quiet, Daniel gave her a small treat. At first, this did not work very well. Pepper still barked most of the time. ( 2 ), Daniel did not give up. He practiced with her every day for two months. Slowly, Pepper learned to sit quietly by the door. Now, she hardly ever barks. Daniel's neighbors have even started bringing treats for Pepper when they visit.

choices: find a way to stop her barking
questions.why: 近所の人が鳴き声に困っていて、次の段落でダニエルは犬のしつけの本を読んでいる。だから両親は「ほえるのをやめさせる方法を見つけて」と言った。
前の「最初はうまくいかず、まだほえていた」と、後ろの「ダニエルはあきらめなかった」は逆の内容なので、逆接の However。As a result（その結果）は因果、For example は例、In other words は言い換え。

sets.passage:
Stars in the Sky

Kaito lives in a big city. At night, the city is so bright that he can see only a few stars. Last summer, Kaito visited his grandfather, who lives in a small village in the mountains. On the first night, his grandfather took him outside after dinner. When Kaito looked up, he was surprised. He could see ( 1 ). His grandfather pointed at some of them and told him their names.

After Kaito went back home, he wanted to learn more about stars. He borrowed books from the library and joined the astronomy club at his school. However, it was difficult to see stars clearly from the city. Then the club's teacher had an idea. She ( 2 ). Now, once a month, the members take a bus to a park far from the city lights and watch the night sky together. Kaito hopes to visit his grandfather again next summer with a telescope.

questions.why: 都会では星が少ししか見えない、という前置きと「驚いた」、直後の「祖父がそのいくつかを指さして名前を教えた」から、たくさんの星が見えたと分かる。月だけ・雲では of them と名前の話に合わない。

choices: bought a new computer for the club
asked the city to make the streets brighter
planned trips to a darker place
told the members to stay at home
questions.why: 直後に「月に1回、街の明かりから遠い公園へバスで行って星を見る」とある。先生のアイデアは暗い場所へ出かけること。街を明るくするのは逆効果。

sets.passage:
Sophie's First Cake

Sophie's mother loves cakes, so Sophie wanted to make one for her mother's birthday. She had never baked anything before, so she asked her aunt, who owns a small bakery, for help. Her aunt said that she was busy on weekdays, but she ( 1 ). On Saturday morning, Sophie went to the bakery early. She was excited but also a little nervous.

Her aunt showed her how to mix the eggs, butter, and sugar. Sophie worked carefully, but when she took the cake out of the oven, it was flat and hard. She felt very sad. Her aunt smiled and said that her own first cake had been even worse. They tried again, and this time ( 2 ). On her mother's birthday, Sophie served the cake with fresh strawberries. Her mother said it was the best present she had ever received. Now, Sophie bakes something for her family every weekend.

questions.why: 「平日は忙しいが～」の but の後は、手伝える日の話。次の文で「土曜の朝、ソフィーは店に行った」とあるので、土曜なら教えられる、が入る。
1回目は失敗したが、もう一度作り、母の誕生日にそのケーキを出して喜ばれた。だから2回目はうまくいった（turn out well＝結果がうまくいく）。

sets.passage:
The School Newspaper

Haruto is a junior high school student who loves writing. In April, he joined the school newspaper club. For his first article, the club leader asked him to write about someone who works at the school. Haruto did not know whom to choose. Then he remembered Mr. Sano, the man who takes care of the school buildings. Every morning, Mr. Sano opened the gates and cleaned the hallways, but Haruto had never ( 1 ).

The next day, Haruto asked Mr. Sano for an interview. Mr. Sano was surprised but happy. He told Haruto that he had worked at the school for thirty years and that he planted all the flowers by the front gate. Haruto's article was printed in the June newspaper. After that, ( 2 ). sets.passage:
Sea Otters: Small Helpers of the Ocean

Sea otters are small animals that live in the cold waters of the northern Pacific Ocean. Unlike most sea animals, they do not have a thick layer of fat to keep them warm. Instead, they have the thickest fur of any animal in the world. They spend several hours each day cleaning their fur, because dirty fur cannot keep them warm.

Sea otters are also famous for being one of the few animals that use tools. When they find a shellfish, they often lie on their backs in the water and put a stone on their stomachs. Then they hit the shellfish against the stone until it breaks open. Some sea otters keep a favorite stone in a pocket of loose skin under their arms and use it again and again. When they sleep, sea otters sometimes hold each other's paws so that they do not float away from their group.

Scientists say that sea otters are important for the ocean environment. They eat large numbers of sea urchins, which are small animals covered in sharp spines. Sea urchins eat kelp, a kind of large seaweed that grows in underwater forests. If there are too many sea urchins, the kelp forests can disappear. These forests are home to many kinds of fish, so they need to be protected.

More than 100 years ago, sea otters were hunted in large numbers for their fur, and they almost disappeared. Laws were later made to protect them, and their numbers slowly increased. However, sea otters still face problems today. For example, oil from ships can make their fur dirty, and this can be very dangerous for them. Many groups are now working to keep the ocean clean so that sea otters can continue to live there safely.

questions.q: How do sea otters stay warm?
choices: They have a thick layer of fat under their skin.
They have very thick fur that they keep clean.
They sleep together in large groups on land.
They swim to warmer waters in winter.
questions.why: 第1段落：脂肪の層は無く、代わりにとても厚い毛皮を持ち、毎日何時間も手入れをする。脂肪の層は「無い」と書かれている。

questions.q: What do some sea otters do with stones?
choices: They throw them at other animals.
They use them to build their homes.
They keep them and use them many times to open shellfish.
They hold them in their paws while they sleep.
questions.why: 第2段落：お気に入りの石を脇の下のたるんだ皮に入れて、何度も使う。寝る時に握るのは石ではなく仲間の前足。

questions.q: Why are sea otters important for kelp forests?
choices: They plant new kelp on the ocean floor.
They keep fish away from the kelp.
They eat sea urchins, which eat kelp.
They clean oil from the water.
questions.why: 第3段落：ラッコはウニを大量に食べる。ウニはケルプを食べるので、ウニが増えすぎるとケルプの森が消えてしまう。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Sea otters are found mostly in warm southern seas.
Sea otters eat large amounts of kelp every day.
Oil from ships helps to keep sea otters' fur clean.
Laws helped the number of sea otters to increase.
questions.why: 第4段落：保護する法律ができて数がゆっくり増えた。ラッコは北太平洋の冷たい海にすみ、ケルプを食べるのはウニ、油は毛皮を汚す。

sets.passage:
The Walking School Bus

In many countries, fewer children walk to school than in the past. Many parents drive their children to school because they worry about busy roads. However, this causes more traffic near schools in the morning, and children get less exercise. To solve these problems, some towns have started an idea called the "walking school bus."

A walking school bus is not really a bus. It is a group of children who walk to school together with one or two adults. Like a real bus, it follows a set route and stops at certain places, such as street corners, at the same time every morning. Children wait at these "bus stops" and join the group as it passes. The adults are usually parents or volunteers from the town, and they make sure that the children cross roads safely.

The town of Maplewood started a walking school bus three years ago. At first, only twelve children joined. Now, more than 150 students at four elementary schools use it. A survey by the town found that the number of cars near the schools in the morning has gone down by about 30 percent. Teachers also say that students who walk to school seem more awake during their first class. Some parents like the program because it gives them more free time in the morning.

However, running a walking school bus is not always easy. The program needs enough adults to walk with the children every day, even in bad weather. In Maplewood, it was sometimes hard to find volunteers on rainy or snowy days. To solve this problem, the town asked retired people to help. Many older residents were happy to join, and they enjoy talking with the children on the way. Now, the town hopes that other towns will learn from its success.

questions.q: Why do many parents drive their children to school?
choices: Schools are too far away to walk to.
Their children do not like to exercise.
There are no buses in their towns.
They are worried about traffic on the roads.
questions.why: 第1段落：交通量の多い道路が心配だから（worry about busy roads）。学校が遠い・運動が嫌い、とは書かれていない。

questions.q: How is a walking school bus similar to a real bus?
choices: It follows a route and stops at fixed places at the same time.
Children have to pay money to use it.
It is driven by parents or volunteers.
It can carry more than 100 children at once.
questions.why: 第2段落：本物のバスのように、決まった道順を通り、毎朝同じ時刻に決まった場所に止まる。大人は一緒に歩くだけで、運転はしない。

questions.q: What has happened in Maplewood since the program began?
choices: Students have to get up much earlier.
Only twelve children use it now.
Teachers walk with the students every day.
There are fewer cars near the schools in the morning.
questions.why: 第3段落：朝の学校付近の車が約30％減った。12人は始めた時の数で、今は150人以上。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Maplewood started the program ten years ago.
The program stops when it rains or snows.
The walking school bus is only for high school students.
Older people in Maplewood now help with the program.
questions.why: 第4段落：雨や雪の日にボランティアが足りず、退職した人たちに頼んだら多くの年配の住民が参加した。始めたのは3年前、対象は小学生。

sets.passage:
Board Game Cafés

Many people today spend their free time looking at screens. They play video games, watch videos, and send messages on their smartphones. However, in recent years, a different kind of entertainment has become popular again in many cities: board games. One sign of this is the growing number of board game cafés.

At a board game café, customers pay a small fee to sit at a table and play as many games as they want. Some cafés have more than 500 games on their shelves. The games range from simple card games for children to difficult strategy games that take several hours to finish. Customers can also order drinks and snacks while they play. Many cafés have staff members called "game guides" who explain the rules, so customers can try new games without reading long instruction books.

People enjoy board game cafés for different reasons. Some say that playing games face to face is more fun than playing online, because they can see each other's reactions and laugh together. Others use the cafés as a place to meet new people. Some cafés hold special events where people who come alone are put into groups with other players. Board games can also be good for the brain. Many games require players to plan ahead, remember information, and make quick decisions.

However, running a board game café can be difficult. Because customers often stay for many hours but order only one or two drinks, it can be hard for cafés to make money. Also, games can get damaged, and small pieces are often lost. To deal with these problems, some cafés set time limits on weekends, while others sell games so that customers can buy their favorite ones to take home. Owners hope that more people will discover the fun of playing games together.

questions.q: What do game guides at board game cafés do?
choices: They explain the rules so customers can try new games easily.
They play every game with the customers.
They make drinks and snacks for customers.
They sell old games at low prices.
questions.why: 第2段落：ゲームガイドはルールを説明するので、客は長い説明書を読まずに新しいゲームを試せる。

questions.q: Why do some people prefer playing games face to face?
choices: Online games cost too much money.
They can see other players' reactions and laugh together.
They do not have their own smartphones.
Board games take less time to finish.
questions.why: 第3段落：対面だとお互いの反応が見えて一緒に笑えるので、オンラインより楽しい。

questions.q: What is one problem for board game cafés?
choices: Customers stay a long time but do not spend much money.
Not enough customers know the rules of games.
New games are too expensive to buy.
Customers often bring their own games.
questions.why: 第4段落：客は何時間もいるのに飲み物を1〜2杯しか頼まないので、もうけを出しにくい。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Most board game cafés have fewer than 50 games.
Board game cafés never allow customers to buy games.
Some cafés hold events where people who come alone can play with others.
Board games cannot help people to think.
questions.why: 第3段落：一人で来た人を他の客とグループにするイベントを開く店がある。500以上のゲームがある店もあり、ゲームを売る店もあり、ゲームは頭に良いとも書かれている。

sets.passage:
The Journey of the Tomato

Today, tomatoes are one of the most popular vegetables in the world. They are used in salads, soups, sauces, and many other dishes. Strictly speaking, though, the tomato is a fruit, because it grows from a flower and contains seeds. Wherever you go, it is easy to find dishes made with tomatoes. However, people did not always love them.

Wild tomatoes first grew in South America. Long ago, people in Central America began growing them as food. The tomatoes they grew were much smaller than the ones we eat today, and many were yellow instead of red. In the 1500s, travelers from Europe brought tomato plants back home with them. At first, many Europeans grew tomatoes only as beautiful plants in their gardens. They did not want to eat them because tomato plants look similar to some plants that are poisonous. For a long time, some people believed that eating tomatoes could make them sick.

Slowly, people's opinions changed. In southern Europe, where the weather is warm and sunny, tomatoes grew very well, and cooks started using them in their dishes. By the 1800s, tomato sauce had become an important part of cooking in many areas. Later, tomatoes became popular in other parts of the world, too. Farmers developed many new kinds of tomatoes in different shapes, sizes, and colors.

Today, scientists are still working to create better tomatoes. Some are trying to grow tomatoes that can survive in hot and dry places where water is limited. Others are developing tomatoes that stay fresh for a longer time so that less food is thrown away. Some people, however, think that modern tomatoes do not taste as good as old kinds. Because of this, a growing number of home gardeners are choosing to grow traditional types of tomatoes from old seeds.

questions.q: What is true about the first tomatoes that people grew as food?
choices: They were smaller than modern tomatoes, and many were yellow.
They were first grown in southern Europe.
They were bigger and redder than today's tomatoes.
They were grown only for their flowers.
questions.why: 第2段落：中央アメリカで育てられたトマトは今よりずっと小さく、多くは赤ではなく黄色だった。ヨーロッパに来たのは1500年代。

questions.q: Why did many Europeans not eat tomatoes at first?
choices: Tomatoes did not grow in their gardens.
They thought that tomatoes might make them sick.
Tomatoes were too expensive to buy.
They did not like the color of tomatoes.
questions.why: 第2段落：トマトが毒のある植物に似ていたので、食べると病気になると信じる人がいた。庭では観賞用に育てていた。

questions.q: What happened in southern Europe?
choices: Farmers grew tomatoes only in winter.
Tomatoes grew well, and cooks started to use them.
Travelers brought tomatoes there from Asia.
People sent tomatoes back to South America.
questions.why: 第3段落：暖かく日当たりのよい南ヨーロッパではトマトがよく育ち、料理人が使い始めた。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Scientists have stopped trying to improve tomatoes.
Everyone agrees that modern tomatoes taste better.
Some home gardeners are growing old types of tomatoes.
Tomatoes are now grown only in South America.
questions.why: 第4段落：今のトマトは昔の品種ほどおいしくないと考える人がいて、古い種から伝統的な品種を育てる家庭菜園の人が増えている。科学者は今も改良を続けている。

sets.passage:
Bees on the Roof

Honeybees are important insects. When they fly from flower to flower to collect nectar, they carry pollen with them. This helps plants to make fruit and seeds. About one third of the food that people eat, such as apples, strawberries, and almonds, depends on bees and other insects. However, in many parts of the world, the number of honeybees has been going down because of disease and the loss of wild flowers.

In recent years, some people in big cities have started keeping bees on the roofs of buildings. This may sound strange, but cities can actually be good places for bees. There are many kinds of flowers in parks, gardens, and along the streets. Also, cities often use fewer chemicals to kill insects than large farms do. Some hotels and office buildings now have beehives on their roofs, and their workers take care of the bees.

Rooftop beekeeping has other good points, too. The honey that city bees make has a special taste because the bees visit many different kinds of flowers. Some hotels use their own honey in their restaurants, and guests enjoy trying it. Schools have also started small beekeeping programs. Students watch the bees closely and learn how insects and plants depend on each other. Many students say that they became less afraid of bees after joining these programs.

However, experts say that people should be careful. If too many hives are put in one area, there may not be enough flowers for all the bees. Then honeybees may take food away from wild bees that also live in the city. For this reason, some cities have made rules about how many hives can be kept on each building. Experts also say that planting more flowers is one of the best ways for anyone to help bees.

questions.q: Why has the number of honeybees been going down?
choices: Because people eat too much honey.
Because cities have become too cold.
Because of disease and fewer wild flowers.
Because farmers no longer grow apples.
questions.why: 第1段落：病気と野生の花が減ったことが原因。リンゴなどは虫に頼る食べ物の例で、原因ではない。

questions.q: What is one reason that cities can be good places for bees?
choices: There are no other insects in cities.
Cities use more chemicals than farms.
There are many kinds of flowers in different places.
questions.why: 第2段落：公園・庭・道ばたにいろいろな花がある。また、都市は大きな農場より殺虫剤が少ない（more ではなく fewer）。

questions.q: What do students learn from school beekeeping programs?
choices: How insects and plants need each other.
How to build roofs for buildings.
How to sell honey to hotels.
questions.why: 第3段落：生徒はハチを観察し、虫と植物がどう頼り合っているかを学ぶ（depend on each other → need each other）。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Experts think every building should have many hives.
Some cities limit the number of hives on each building.
City honey tastes the same as other honey.
Wild bees cannot live in cities.
questions.why: 第4段落：建物ごとに置ける巣箱の数のルールを作った都市がある。巣箱が多すぎると花が足りなくなると専門家は注意している。都市のハチミツは特別な味。

sets.passage:
Libraries of Things

Most people know that they can borrow books from a library. But what about a drill, a tent, or a sewing machine? In some towns, people can now borrow these things from a place called a "library of things." These libraries lend all kinds of useful items that people need only once in a while, such as tools, camping equipment, and kitchen machines. Some of them have more than a thousand items on their shelves.

The idea is simple. Members usually pay a small fee each year, and then they can borrow items for a few days or a week. For example, a family that is going camping for the first time can borrow a tent and sleeping bags instead of buying them. Someone who wants to hang a picture can borrow a drill for one afternoon. Many libraries of things are run by volunteers, and some are inside regular public libraries.

There are several reasons why these libraries are becoming popular. First, they help people save money. Many tools are expensive, but people often use them only a few times. Second, they are good for the environment. When many people share one item, fewer things need to be made and thrown away. Third, they bring people together. Some libraries hold classes where volunteers teach members how to repair bikes or use tools safely.

However, running a library of things is not always easy. Items sometimes come back broken or dirty, and volunteers have to spend time fixing and cleaning them. Some members also forget to return things on time. To deal with these problems, many libraries check each item carefully when it is returned and send reminders by e-mail. People who run these libraries hope that, in the future, sharing things will become as normal as sharing books.

questions.q: What kind of things does a library of things lend?
choices: Useful items that people do not need very often.
New items that people must buy later.
questions.why: 第1段落：工具やキャンプ用品など、たまにしか必要としない便利な物を貸す（once in a while → not very often）。

questions.q: What is one example given in the passage?
choices: A family can buy a tent at a low price.
Members can keep items for one year.
A family can borrow a tent for a first camping trip.
A volunteer can sell a drill to a member.
questions.why: 第2段落：初めてキャンプに行く家族は、買わずにテントと寝袋を借りられる。年に払うのは会費で、借りられるのは数日〜1週間。

questions.q: How do libraries of things help the environment?
choices: They teach people how to grow vegetables.
They plant trees with the money from members.
When people share items, fewer things are made and thrown away.
questions.why: 第3段落：たくさんの人で1つの物を共有すると、作られて捨てられる物が減る。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Some libraries send e-mails to remind members to return items.
Items always come back clean and in good condition.
Libraries of things never have classes.
Members do not need to pay anything.
questions.why: 第4段落：返し忘れ対策として、メールでお知らせを送る図書館が多い。壊れたり汚れたりして返ってくることもあり、修理の教室もあり、会費は少額かかる。

sets.passage:
Clever Octopuses

Octopuses are sea animals with eight long arms and no bones. They live in oceans all around the world, from warm, shallow waters to the cold, deep sea. Although they are related to snails and clams, octopuses are known as some of the most intelligent animals in the ocean. Scientists have been studying them for many years to learn how they think.

One amazing thing about octopuses is that they can change the color of their skin in less than a second. They use this ability to hide from enemies and to catch fish and crabs. Some octopuses can even change the shape of their skin so that they look like rocks or plants. If an enemy finds them, octopuses can also shoot out a cloud of black ink. While the enemy cannot see, the octopus swims away.

Octopuses are also very good at solving problems. In one experiment, scientists put a crab inside a glass jar with a lid. An octopus soon learned how to open the lid to get the crab. Some octopuses that live in aquariums have escaped from their tanks at night. They traveled to other tanks to eat fish and then returned to their own tanks before the workers came in the morning. Scientists have also found that octopuses can tell the difference between people who feed them and people who do not.

However, octopuses do not live very long. Most kinds live for only one or two years. Female octopuses lay thousands of eggs and guard them carefully, often without eating. After the babies come out, the mother usually dies. Because octopuses live such short lives, scientists are surprised by how much they can learn in a short time. They hope that studying octopuses will help us understand more about how brains work.

questions.q: What is true about where octopuses live?
choices: They live in rivers and lakes.
They can be found in both warm and cold oceans.
They live on land near the sea.
They live only in warm, shallow water.
questions.why: 第1段落：暖かい浅い海から冷たい深海まで、世界中の海にすんでいる。浅い海「だけ」ではない。

questions.q: How do octopuses escape from enemies?
choices: They call other octopuses for help.
They run away on the sea floor very fast.
They shoot out ink so that enemies cannot see.
questions.why: 第2段落：敵に見つかると黒い墨を吐き、敵が見えない間に泳いで逃げる。ガラスのびんは実験の話。

questions.q: What did some octopuses in aquariums do?
choices: They left their tanks at night to eat fish in other tanks.
They opened the doors of the aquarium.
They changed color to show workers they were hungry.
questions.why: 第3段落：夜に水槽から抜け出してほかの水槽の魚を食べ、朝になる前に戻っていた。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Octopuses have strong bones in their arms.
Female octopuses eat a lot while guarding their eggs.
Most octopuses live for only a short time.
questions.why: 第4段落：ほとんどの種類は1〜2年しか生きない。骨は無く、メスは卵を守る間ほとんど食べず、科学者は今も研究している。

sets.passage:
Farms in Tall Buildings

As the number of people in cities grows, more and more food is needed. Usually, vegetables are grown on farms in the countryside and then carried to cities by truck. This can take several days, and some vegetables are no longer fresh when they arrive. To solve this problem, some companies have started growing vegetables inside buildings in the middle of cities. These are called vertical farms.

In a vertical farm, plants are grown on shelves that are stacked one on top of another, sometimes ten or more levels high. The plants do not grow in soil. Instead, their roots are kept in water that contains everything they need. Special lights are used instead of sunlight, and computers control the temperature and the amount of water. Lettuce, herbs, and strawberries are some of the most common crops grown this way. Some vertical farms are even built inside old factories that are no longer used.

Vertical farms have many good points. Because the plants are grown indoors, farmers do not have to worry about bad weather or insects, so they can harvest vegetables all year round. They also use much less water than traditional farms, because the water can be used again and again. In addition, the vegetables can be sold in stores near the farm on the same day that they are picked.

However, vertical farms also have some problems. The special lights and computers use a lot of electricity, so the farms can be expensive to run. Also, it is difficult to grow large plants such as corn or potatoes on shelves. For these reasons, vertical farms will probably not replace traditional farms. Still, many people believe that they can be an important way to bring fresh food to people in cities.

questions.q: Why do some vegetables lose their freshness?
choices: It can take days to carry them from farms to cities.
Stores keep them for too long.
They are grown under special lights.
questions.why: 第1段落：田舎の農場からトラックで都市へ運ぶのに数日かかることがあり、着いた時には新鮮でない。

questions.q: How are plants grown in a vertical farm?
choices: In soil on the roofs of houses.
On shelves with their roots in water.
In large fields in the countryside.
questions.why: 第2段落：何段にも重ねた棚で、土ではなく栄養の入った水に根をつけて育てる。日光の代わりに特別なライトを使う。

questions.q: What is one good point of vertical farms?
choices: They do not need any electricity.
They can grow every kind of vegetable.
They need more water than other farms.
Farmers can harvest vegetables in any season.
questions.why: 第3段落：屋内なので天気や虫を気にせず、1年中収穫できる（all year round → in any season）。水は少なくて済み、電気はたくさん使う。

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
choices: Vertical farms are cheap to run.
It is hard to grow large plants like corn in vertical farms.
Vertical farms will soon replace all traditional farms.
Lettuce cannot be grown in vertical farms.
questions.why: 第4段落：トウモロコシやジャガイモのような大きな作物は棚で育てにくい。電気代が高く、従来の農場に取って代わることはないだろう、とある。

parts.title: ライティング Eメール返信
parts.desc: 知り合いからのEメール（約85語）に返信し、質問に答えて下線部について2つ質問する（40〜50語）
parts.tip: 型を決める：① Thank you の後に質問への答え（I think ～. because ～.）② 下線部について具体的な質問を2つ（How much ～? / How many ～?）。答えと質問の両方が無いと大きく減点。50語を超えないよう、理由は1つで短く。
parts.intro: Read the e-mail from Alex. Write a reply that answers Alex's question and asks two questions about the underlined part.

sets.prompt:
●外国人の知り合い（Alex）からEメールが届きました。メールの中の質問に答える返信を、英語で書いてください。
●返信の中に、Alex のメールの下線部について、どんな物なのかをもっとよく知るための具体的な質問を2つ入れてください。
●語数の目安は40〜50語です。Best wishes, の後に自分の名前は書かなくてかまいません。

Hi!
I have some news. Last weekend, my family bought <u>a robot vacuum cleaner</u>. It cleans the floors by itself while we are out, so my parents are very happy. However, my little brother is a bit afraid of it, because it moves around the house and makes strange noises. My father says that robots will do much more housework in the future. Do you think more people will use robots to do housework in the future?
Your friend,
Alex
sets.note: 書き出しは「Hi, Alex! Thank you for your e-mail.」、結びは「Best wishes,」（どちらも語数に数えない）。質問（ロボットが家事をするようになるか）への答えを理由付きで1〜2文。ロボット掃除機について、値段・大きさ・使い方などの具体的な質問を2つ（How much was it? / How long does it take to clean the house?）。

parts.title: ライティング 英作文（意見）
parts.desc: QUESTION に対する意見と理由2つを50〜60語で書く
parts.tip: 型を決めておく：I think ～. I have two reasons. First, ～. Second, ～. For these reasons, ～. 理由は「何が・どう良いか」まで具体的に。難しい語より、間違えない語で。
parts.intro: Read the QUESTION. Write your opinion and give two reasons for it.

sets.prompt:
●外国人の知り合いから、次の QUESTION をされました。
●QUESTION について、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英語で書いてください。
●語数の目安は50〜60語です。

QUESTION
Do you think it is a good idea for students to study at the library after school?
sets.note: Give two reasons. 最初に意見（Yes / No か、どちらか）。理由を2つ、それぞれ1〜2文で支え、最後にもう一度意見。理由の例：家より集中できる・本や辞書が使える／移動に時間がかかる・友達と話してしまう、など。
